rationale_given:
P-A' (chmod 1770) was independently verified in 149O.20L.7O.2A.1 as the minimum-safe current-architecture remediation for the RepositoryIdentity write-path provisioning gap on hac-dell. Intent: allow the pcae OS principal to create legitimate runtime-local .pcae artifacts via mkstemp+os.replace/exclusive-create idioms; preserve existing root ownership of all 17 tracked governed .pcae entries; rely on Linux sticky-directory semantics (S_ISVTX, kernel check_sticky()/may_delete() in fs/namei.c) to prevent the non-owner pcae group member from unlinking, renaming, or rename-replacing existing root-owned files; keep the Protected Root /etc/pcae/hatp/trust-store entirely unaffected (no shared filesystem ancestor). 1770 does not make .pcae generally trusted or authority-bearing; the only authority-relevant consumer of anything under .pcae/ is HBDC-REQ-042 (_check_deployment_identity), which cross-checks against the Protected Root, not against .pcae/'s own mode.

Required disclosed correction (carried forward from 7O.2A.1 SS5/SS11/SS32, independently re-confirmed this phase): P-A' correctly fixes the write-path provisioning problem for 38 of the 39 declared write-required .pcae artifacts (the .gitignore-declared set). It does NOT fix architecture-history.json, whose producer (write_architecture_history_snapshot, architecture.py) uses a direct truncating open("w") on a pre-existing, root-owned 0640 file rather than the mkstemp+os.replace atomic-create idiom repository_identity.py uses -- a directory-mode-only change cannot grant write access denied by the file's own mode bits. That artifact's fix is a separate, not-yet-designed producer change, out of this proposition's scope and deferred. This election does not claim P-A' covers the complete write-required inventory.

Sticky-bit evidence qualification (carried forward, tier-tagged per 7O.2A.1 SS1/SS8): the sticky-bit protection relied upon is REFERENCE-VERIFIED FROM PRIMARY LINUX/POSIX SOURCES (S_ISVTX, POSIX/SUSv4-mandated, identical mechanism to /tmp's own long-standing 1777 behavior on every mainstream Linux distribution) -- it was not empirically tested by creating synthetic root-owned files on hac-dell during 7O.2A.1, because that phase prohibited Dell mutation, and this phase (7O.2A.2) is election/publication-only and performs zero Dell mutation as well. This is an evidence qualification, not a blocking finding.

Fresh HBDC re-check performed this phase, live, read-only, via sudo -n -u pcae under the canonical corrected Action-9 environment (env -i reset, PATH=/opt/pcae/runtime/venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin, HOME=/home/pcae, PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, cwd=/opt/pcae/runtime/src): status NON_COMPLIANT, sole residual HBDC-REQ-042 (no_repository_identity_present); HBDC-REQ-036 independently confirmed True (launcher_agent_unwritable) under the same canonical invocation. Matches the expected baseline exactly -- proceeded to election, no STOP.
